entry_point.discipline_context: Potential energy, equilibrium configurations, and numerical relaxation in mechanical engineering.
entry_point.rationale: These ideas give students an intuitive entry to stationary points, descent directions, curvature, and conditioning before formal algorithm comparisons.
entry_point.analogy_boundary: The energy picture is a teaching analogy: an optimisation objective need not be physical energy, and an algorithmic iterate is not automatically a physical time state.

conditional_item_decisions.rationale: Exact line search is a useful contrast with fixed and backtracking steps.
Armijo backtracking is a practical step-selection bridge.

chapter_sequence.title: From equilibrium to an optimisation problem
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce unconstrained objectives, stationarity, and first- and second-order local tests through a careful mechanical entry point.

chapter_sequence.title: Smoothness, convexity, and conditioning
chapter_sequence.purpose: Build the assumptions that control local models, global lower bounds, curvature, and difficulty.

chapter_sequence.title: Gradient descent and choosing a step
chapter_sequence.purpose: State the standard update and compare constant, exact-line-search, and Armijo choices.

chapter_sequence.title: What convergence guarantees actually assume
chapter_sequence.purpose: Interpret the convex and strongly convex GD rates and connect them to conditioning.

chapter_sequence.title: Momentum and acceleration
chapter_sequence.purpose: Contrast Heavy Ball and the specified NAG recurrence, including their precise scope.

chapter_sequence.title: Stochastic and adaptive updates
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce stochastic-gradient assumptions, SGD step schedules, and AdaGrad, RMSProp, and Adam semantics.

chapter_sequence.title: Newton and quasi-Newton methods
chapter_sequence.purpose: Use a second-order Taylor model to motivate Newton, then explain BFGS as curvature learning.

chapter_sequence.title: Turning update rules into reliable Python
chapter_sequence.purpose: Connect mathematical indexing, state variables, diagnostics, and method choice in implementation.

implementation_strategy: Use explicit NumPy state updates, make initialisation and indexing visible, solve Newton systems rather than forming inverses, and diagnose sign, look-ahead, accumulator, and bias-correction errors.
assessment_strategy: Use one theorem-scope check, one deterministic hand calculation with objective-gradient consistency, and one executable Python diagnostic, followed by independent semantic review.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Identify which hypotheses are needed before applying the convex and strongly convex GD rates.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Decide whether a relaxation estimate for a compliant mechanism is justified by the stated objective properties.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Compute a gradient-descent step and verify that the stated gradient comes from the objective.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Relax a two-coordinate quadratic surrogate for a mechanical configuration.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Find and correct an implementation that evaluates standard GD at the wrong state and uses the wrong descent sign.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Inspect a NumPy relaxation loop used for a discretised design variable.
